Select this option to disable original monorail and maglev engines and wagons. Not applicable to normal track trains.
Keep old vehicles in purchase menu

Select this option to disable expiration of old engines and wagons. Historical vehicles will remain available in purchase menu also in modern ages. This option applies only to this set. To disable expiration of another vehicles use option "Vehicles never expire" in game settings.

Some wagons in the set are dedicated to transport special cargoes, defined by FIRS and ECS industry sets. If you play without FIRS and ECS, these wagons are disabled. Select this option to use these wagons with a standard 'goods' cargo.
Use original introduction dates for early rolling stock

Select this option to use original introduction dates for early PKP rolling stock instead of 1918 - the year in which Poland regained its independence.When option is enabled, the first vehicles are available in 1882.

Some multiple units included in this set have very long consists in prototypical usage (e.g. Eurostar).Alter this parameter to set the maximum length in tiles for these longer units.
Running cost penalty for old trains

When trains reach the end of their working life they will become more expensive to run.Higher settings cause this this to happen faster and the increase in costs to be larger.For casual network games and other situations where players may not be able to replace expired vehicles for several decades, �Mild� is recommended as it will still allow most well-designed networks to break even or return a small profit.

When a locomotive gets old, some freight wagons will show weathering and graffiti as an indication it is reaching the end of its life, with more graffiti the older it gets.As this may be visually distracting, you can switch off the accumulation of graffiti over a train with this parameter.
Use company colours for brake vans
By default, brake vans are shown in a variety of prototypical real-world colours to make them visually distinct from freight vehicles. This option allows showing them in company colours instead.

When using extreme sized maps with slow economy speeds (e.g. in JGRPP) the default cargo payment algorithm does not scale well to long train routes. This parameter allows slowing down cargo payment decay to allow more satisfying gameplay on extreme map sizes.�Note:� will make the game significantly easier - you may wish to increase running costs to compensate.

The 1960s rationalisation of BR resulted in a number of sectors abandoned to road transport. Since players may wish to explore the possibilities had BR continued to provide these types of traffic, a number of plausible fictional vehicles are included in this set. For extra realism, these can be turned off with this flag.
